the expression of anti English sentiment in sport is a complex and multi-faceted phenomenon, with a wide range of social, historical, political and personal factors influencing the extent to which such sentiment is expressed.

the expression of anti‐English sentiment by Scots living in Scotland is a result of their ‘ontological narrative’ of Scottishness, which is legitimised by a ‘public narrative’ of Scotland as an underdog in relation to England.

the expression of antiEnglish sentiment is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon, and that a more nuanced understanding is required to appreciate the reasons behind such expression, particularly in relation to the influence of migration to England upon members of the Scottish Diaspora.
The main takeaway from our work is that

anti-English sentiment is not a fixed or static part of Scottish identity but is instead something which is expressed by Scots in relation both to the context in which such sentiments are expressed and to the individual’s own ontological narrative.

the expression of anti‐English sentiment is not simply a product of the ‘othering’ of Englishness in Scotland, but rather is part of an ‘othering’ process that is also present in England, with Englishness being ‘othered’ in England as part of the ‘ontological narrative’ of some English people.

anti-English sentiment is a complex phenomenon that cannot be reduced to a simple binary of ‘Scottish’ versus ‘English’, but rather needs to be understood as part of the broader context of Scottish national identity.
